subject: Urgent: EU capacity hotspot cascade — initial customer notice & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot S. <elliot.s@glyphtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-17 09:12 -0700
Subject: Urgent: EU capacity hotspot cascade — initial customer notice & next steps

Elliot —

Quick heads up: starting ~08:45 UTC this morning we observed a rapid capacity degradation affecting your dedicated pool in eu-west-1. Symptoms we saw: elevated enqueue times, tail latency spikes, and a small percentage of 5xx responses for short-running inference requests.

Our on-call team has identified the primary signal as an autoscaler thrash combined with warmup heuristics that failed to maintain headroom during a burst from your tenant. We have engineers working the remediation now and have applied an immediate mitigation (soft cap on concurrent warmups and a targeted node restart).

What we’re doing next (short term):
- Stabilize routing and put a temporary throughput cap to prevent re-triggering the thrash.
- Apply a hotfix to the warmup heuristic and restart a subset of nodes to re-balance KV caches.
- Collect a timeline and logs for your review.

We’ll follow up with a clearer remediation timeline and a proposed credit/compensation for impacted time. Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts customer latency and throughput.

I’ll send an update within the hour.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: glyphtech_initial_timeline.txt (text), referenced ops notes
From: Elliot S. <elliot.s@glyphtech.com>

Date: 2026-10-17 09:21 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: EU capacity hotspot cascade — initial customer notice & next steps

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick note. We started getting HTTP 502/503 errors around 08:46 UTC and page load times spiked across our EU users. Can you confirm: how long do you expect the mitigation to take? We have a marketing push running and this is time-sensitive. Also: what data/logs will you share for our SRE team to correlate?

Elliot
Head of Platform, GlyphTech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: Elliot S. <elliot.s@glyphtech.com>
Date: 2026-10-17 09:45 -0700
Subject: RE: Urgent: EU capacity hotspot cascade — initial customer notice & next steps

Elliot / Jordan —

Quick technical update from the response team (preliminary):

Root cause (initial hypothesis):
- We observed a kernel-level serialization in our allocator under certain warmup sequences. When GlyphTech’s burst pattern hit the cluster, warmup threads exhausted headroom and the autoscaler entered a thrash state (rapid scale up/down), which amplified resource contention.

Actions completed (09:10 - 09:40 UTC):
- Deployed a hotfix that introduces a conservative warmup ramp and prevents concurrent full-KV cache rebuilds.
- Rebalanced traffic away from the hottest nodes and restarted 6 nodes in the affected pool to flush transient cache skew.
- Temporarily constrained warmup concurrency for GlyphTech to reduce spike amplification.

Current status:
- Error rate has dropped to baseline for most endpoints; tail latency improved but a small fraction of requests are still experiencing degraded latency while caches repopulate.
- Full steady-state expected within 90–120 minutes after cache repopulation completes.

Follow-ups we need from GlyphTech to accelerate troubleshooting:
- Sample request IDs for requests showing 5xxs (if you have them).
- Confirmation of any traffic anomalies on your side (campaigns, client SDK rollout).

Planned next steps (tomorrow):
- Schedule a maintenance window for node-level kernel patching (requires brief rolling reboots).
- Produce a post-incident timeline and provide the log bundle (redacted for PII) and an ops-runbook describing the fix.

We’ll also propose a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Ben, can you prepare a preliminary credit calculation and approval path?

Marissa Cole
Principal Incident Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hotfix-rollback-logs.zip (contains targeted restart logs, node heartbeats)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot S. <elliot.s@glyphtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-17 10:55 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary, proposed remediation window, and credits

Elliot —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise post-incident summary and a proposed schedule for the kernel patch maintenance:
- Incident window (observed): 2026-10-17 08:45–09:30 UTC
- Primary impact: elevated tail latency and transient 5xxs; peak customer-facing error rate approx 2.7% for ~18 minutes
- Mitigation performed: hotfix to warmup ramp, targeted node restarts, temporary warmup concurrency cap
- Estimated time to full steady state: 90–120 minutes after our last restart (we reached near-baseline by 10:00 UTC)

Proposed maintenance to prevent recurrence:
- Target window: 2026-10-20 02:00–03:00 UTC (rolling restarts across eu-west-1 pool, expected <5% traffic shift per minute)
- Expected customer impact: sub-second increase in 99th percentile during individual node restarts; we will route traffic away from restarts and provide live progress updates.

Compensation proposal:
- We propose a credit equal to 2x your expected per-minute usage cost during the 18-minute high-impact window (document attached: customer_credit_proposal.pdf). Ben is standing by to finalize and route for approval.

Next deliverables we’ll share by EOD: timeline PDF, redacted logs bundle, and a short runbook describing the fix and long-term mitigations (improved warmup algorithm + autoscaler hysteresis).

If that schedule works, please confirm and we’ll lock the maintenance. If you need an earlier patch window, we can prioritize but may need to coordinate support hours.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: customer_credit_proposal.pdf, timeline (link)
From: Elliot S. <elliot.s@glyphtech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, ops@glyphtech.com
Date: 2026-10-18 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary, proposed remediation window, and credits

Jordan / Marissa / Ben —

Appreciate the clear update and the proposed credit. Confirming: the October 20 maintenance window works for us — please proceed and give a 24-hour notice prior to action start. We’ll also send a short list of sample request IDs and internal traffic notes by EOD today to help correlation.

Also: for our compliance team, could you include a brief statement about whether any customer prompt/query data was ever written to long-term storage during the incident window? If yes, what retention policies applied?

Ben — I’m copying you directly to coordinate the credit paperwork.

Thanks,
Elliot
Head of Platform, GlyphTech
